about: Rules a generated hex-tile design must keep (lab/design/constraints.py). Unlike design-rules.json, which only warns in the Fusion panel, a failed 'block' constraint drops a design at the gate; 'warn' shows with it. Each names its evidence; a verdict that contradicts one updates or retires it.

constraints.reason: nothing joins or touches within 1.6 mm of the skin
constraints.source: hex-tile skill, 'Keep the skin clear'; the same limit as design-rules.json

constraints.reason: two printed lines, so the skin prints as a real wall
two printed lines, so the side walls print as real walls
two printed lines, so the land prints as a real wall
two printed lines, so the roof plate prints as a real wall
sparse infill close behind the face likely prints through as dashes and diagonal stripes; a narrow band where two walls meet at an angle is allowed and left to the slice risk predictor
constraints.source: E-026 hypothesis and AI-photo reading (RIFT top band, 15.6 mm of grid behind the face); 5 Nov section analysis: v4's solid roof left a ~10 mm band, v6's roof plate meeting the skin leaves 2.2 mm

constraints.reason: the top wall over the hollow roof prints solid only when the top and bottom shell layers fill it; otherwise sparse infill sits just below the top edge (raise bottom_shell_layers, or thin the wall)
constraints.source: 5 Nov analysis: a 2.4 mm wall under 5 top + 3 bottom shells at 0.2 mm leaves about 0.8 mm of sparse infill

constraints.reason: the lettering stays on the land, clear of its edges and the open top
constraints.source: Fusion lettering, 5 Nov 2026 (letters 2.7 mm clear at land_width 17.7, 1.4 mm at 15, 0.9 mm at 14)
